summary: @nestjs-passport/jwt ships a 2.3MB JSFuck payload executed via new Function() at import time
details: Package is advertised as a minimal HS256 JWT helper around `jose` but ships a 2.3MB single-line bundle whose entire body is a JSFuck expression (composed only of `[]()!+`) passed to `new Function('jose',...)` and invoked at module load. Both CJS (`dist/index.cjs`) and ESM (`dist/index.js`) entrypoints share this shape, and the shipped `dist/index.d.ts` leaks obfuscated private field names such as `_0x5f2e` and `_0x4b19`. Any consumer that `require`s or imports the package executes the opaque payload with full Node privileges. No sourcemap or readable strings are shipped, and standard deobfuscation exhausts the stack. The scope `@nestjs-passport` resembles the official `@nestjs/*` scope. A minimal `jose` wrapper has no legitimate reason to be JSFuck-encoded and dispatched through dynamic `Function` evaluation; this shape is a load-time arbitrary-code-execution loader hiding its semantics from consumers and scanners.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
